1.1: The word of the Lord, which came unto Zephaniah ye sonne of Cushi, the sonne of Gedaliah, the sonne of Amariah, the sonne of Hizkiah, in the dayes of Josiah, the sonne of Amon King of Judah.
1.2: I will surely destroy all things from off the land, saith the Lord.
1.3: I will destroy man and beast: I wil destroy the foules of the heaven, and the fishes of the sea, and ruines shalbe to the wicked, and I will cut off man from off the land, saith the Lord.
1.4: I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and I wil cut off the remnant of Baal from this place, and the name of the Chemarims with ye Priestes,
1.5: And them that worship the host of heaven upon the house tops, and them that worship and swear by the Lord, and swear by Malcham,
1.6: And them that are turned back from the Lord, and those that have not sought the Lord, nor inquired for him.
1.7: Be stil at the presence of the Lord God: for the day of the Lord is at hand: for the Lord hath prepared a sacrifice, and hath sanctified his ghests.
1.8: And it shalbe in the day of the Lords sacrifice, that I will visit the princes and the Kings children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparell.
1.9: In the same day also will I visit all those that dance upon the threshold so proudly, which fill their masters houses by crueltie and deceit.
1.10: And in that day, saith the Lord, there shall be a noise, and cry from the fishgate, and an howling from the second gate, and a great destruction from the hilles.
1.11: Howl ye inhabitants of the low place: for the companie of the marchants is destroyed: all they that bear silver, are cut off.
1.12: And at that time will I search Jerusalem with lightes, and visit the men that are frosen in their dregges, and say in their heartes, The Lord will neither doe good nor doe evil.
1.13: Therefore their goods shall be spoyled, and their houses waste: they shall also build houses, but not inhabit them, and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof.
1.14: The great day of the Lord is neere: it is neere, and hasteth greatly, even the voyce of the day of the Lord: the strong man shall cry there bitterly.
1.15: That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and heaviness, a day of destruction and desolation, a day of obscuritie and darkenesse, a day of cloudes and blackenesse,
1.16: A day of the trumpet and alarm against the strong cities, and against the hie towres.
1.17: And I will bring distress upon men, that they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the Lord, and their blood shall be powred out as dust, and their flesh as the dongue.
1.18: Neither their silver nor their gold shalbe able to deliver them in ye day of the Lords wrath, but the whole land shalbe deuoured by the fire of his ielousie: for hee shall make even a speedie riddance of all them that dwell in the land.

2.1: Gather your selves, even gather you, O nation not worthie to be loved,
2.2: Before the decree come foorth, and ye be as chaff that passeth in a day, and before the fierce wrath of the Lord come upon you, and before the day of the Lords anger come upon you.
2.3: Seek yee the Lord all the meek of the earth, which have wrought his iudgement: seek righteousness, seek lowliness, if so bee that ye may be hid in the day of the Lords wrath.
2.4: For Azzah shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon desolate: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shalbe rooted up.
2.5: Wo unto the inhabitants of the sea coast. the nation of the Cherethims, the word of the Lord is against you: O Canaan, the land of the Philistims, I will even destroy thee without an inhabitant.
2.6: And the sea coast shall be dwellings and cotages for shepheardes and sheepefoldes.
2.7: And that coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah, to feed thereupon: in the houses of Ashkelon shall they lodge toward night: for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captiuitie.
2.8: I have heard the reproch of Moab, and the rebukes of the children of Ammon, whereby they upbraided my people, and magnified themselves against their borders.
2.9: Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall bee as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorah, even the breeding of nettels and salt pittes, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my folk shall spoyle them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.
2.10: This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproched and magnified themselves against the Lord of hostes people.
2.11: The Lord will be terrible unto them: for he wil consume all the gods of the earth, and every man shall worship him from his place, even all the yles of the heathen.
2.12: Ye Morians also shalbe slain by my sword with them.
2.13: And he wil stretch out his hand against the North, and destroy Asshur, and will make Nineveh desolate, and waste like a wilderness.
2.14: And flockes shall lie in the middes of her, and all the beastes of the nations, and the pelican, and the owl shall abide in the upper postes of it: the voyce of birdes shall sing in the windowes, and desolations shalbe upon the postes: for the cedars are vncouered.
2.15: This is the reioycing citie that dwelt careless, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none besides me: how is she made waste, and the lodging of the beastes! every one that passeth by her, shall hiss and wagge his hand.

3.1: Woe to her that is filthie and polluted, to the robbing citie.
3.2: She heard not the voyce: she received not correction: she trusted not in the Lord: she drew not neere to her God.
3.3: Her princes within her are as roaring lyons: her judges are as wolves in the evening, which leave not the bones till the morow.
3.4: Her prophets are light, and wicked persons: her priests have polluted the Sanctuarie: they have wrested the Law.
3.5: The just Lord is in the middes thereof: he will doe none iniquitie: every morning doeth hee bring his iudgement to light, he faileth not: but the wicked will not learn to be ashamed.
3.6: I have cut off the nations: their towres are desolate: I have made their streetes waste, that none shall pass by: their cities are destroyed without man and without inhabitant.
3.7: I said, Surely thou wilt fear me: thou wilt receive instruction: so their dwelling should not be destroyed howsoever I visited them, but they rose earely and corrupted all their workes.
3.8: Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the Lord, until the day that I rise up to the pray: for I am determined to gather the nations, and that I will assemble the kingdomes to powre upon them mine indignation, even all my fierce wrath: for all the earth shall be deuoured with the fire of my ielousie.
3.9: Surely then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the Name of the Lord, to serve him with one cosent.
3.10: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, the daughter of my dispersed, praying unto me, shall bring me an offering.
3.11: In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy workes, wherein thou hast transgressed against mee: for then I will take away out of the middes of thee them that reioyce of thy pride, and thou shalt no more be proud of mine holy Mountain.
3.12: Then will I leave in the middes of thee an humble and poor people: and they shall trust in the Name of the Lord.
3.13: The remnant of Israel shall do none iniquitie, nor speak lies: neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shalbe fed, and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.
3.14: Reioyce, O daughter Zion: be ye ioyfull, O Israel: be glad and reioyce with all thine heart, O daughter Jerusalem.
3.15: The Lord hath taken away thy iudgements: hee hath cast out thine enemie: the King of Israel, even the Lord is in the middes of thee: thou shalt see no more evil.
3.16: In that day it shalbe said to Jerusalem, Fear thou not, O Zion: let not thine handes be faint.
3.17: The Lord thy God in the middes of thee is mightie: hee will save, hee will reioyce over thee with ioye: he will quiet himself in his love: he will reioyce over thee with joy.
3.18: After a certain time will I gather the afflicted that were of thee, and them that bare the reproch for it.
3.19: Behold, at that time I will bruise all that afflict thee, and I will save her that halteth, and gather her that was cast out, and I will get them praise and fame in all the landes of their shame.
3.20: At that time wil I bring you again, and then wil I gather you: for I wil give you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captiuitie before your eyes, saith the Lord.

36:1:3: Not that God was angry with these dumb creatures, but because man was so wicked for whose cause they were created, God maketh them to take part of the punishments with him.
36:1:4: Which were an order of superstitious priests appointed to minister in the service of Baal, and were as his peculiar chaplains, read 2 Kings 23:5; Hos. 10:5.
36:1:5: He alludeth to their idol Molech which was forbidden, Lev. 20:2, yet they called him, their king, and made him as a god: therefore he here noteth them that will both say they worship God, and yet will swear by idols and serve them: which halting is here condemned, as Ezek. 20:39; 1 Kings 18:21; 2 Kings 17:33.
36:1:8: Meaning, the courtiers, which did imitate the strange apparel of other nations to win their favor thereby, and to appear glorious in the eyes of all others, read Ezek. 23:14, 15.
36:1:9: He meaneth the servants of the rulers which invade other men’s houses, and rejoice and leap for joy, when they can get any prey to please their master withall.
36:1:10: Signifying, that all the corners of the city of Jerusalem should be full of trouble.
36:1:11: This is meant of the street of the merchants which was lower than the rest of the place about it.
36:1:12: So that nothing shall escape me.
By their prosperity they are hardened in their wickedness.
36:1:14: They that trusted in their own strength and contemned the Prophets of God.
36:2:1: He exhorteth them to repentance, and willeth them to descend into themselves and gather themselves, lest they be scattered like chaff.
36:2:3: That is, which have lived uprightly and godly according as he prescribeth by his word.
36:2:4: He comforteth the faithful in that God would change his punishments from them unto the Philistines their enemies and other nations.
36:2:5: That is, Galilee: by these nations he meaneth the people that dwelt near to the Jews, and instead of friendship were their enemies: therefore he calleth them Canaanites whom the Lord appointed to be slain.
36:2:7: He showeth why God would destroy their enemies, because their country might be a resting place for his Church.
36:2:8: These nations presumed to take from the Jews that country which the Lord had given them.
36:2:11: When he shall deliver his people and destroy their enemies and Idols, his glory shall shine throughout all the world.
36:2:15: Meaning, Nineveh, which rejoicing so much of her strength and prosperity, should be thus made waste, and God’s people delivered.
36:3:3: They are so greedy that they eat up bones and all.
36:3:5: The wicked thus boasted that God was ever among them, but the Prophet answereth that that cannot excuse their wickedness: for God will not bear with their sins: yet that he did patiently abide and sent his Prophets continually to call them to repentance, but he profited nothing.
36:3:6: By the destruction of other nations he showeth that the Jews should have learned to fear God.
36:3:7: They were most earnest and ready to do wickedly.
36:3:8: Seeing ye will not repent, you shall look for my vengeance as well as other nations.
36:3:9: Hebrew, with one shoulder, as Hos. 6:9.
Lest any should think then that God’s glory should have perished when Judah was destroyed, he showeth that he will publish his grace through all the world.
36:3:10: That is, the Jews shall come as well as the Gentiles: which is to be understood under the time of the Gospel.
36:3:11: For they shall have full remission of their sins, and the hypocrites which boasted of the Temple, which was also thy pride in times past, shall be taken from thee.
36:3:15: That is, the punishment for thy sin.
As the Assyrians, Chaldeans, Egyptians and other nations.
To defend thee as by thy sins thou hast put him away, and left thyself naked, as Exod. 32:25.
36:3:17: Signifying, that God delighteth to show his love and great affection toward his Church.
36:3:18: That is, them that were had in hatred and reviled for the Church, and because of their religion.
36:3:19: I will deliver the Church, which now is afflicted, as Mic. 4:6.
As among the Assyrians and Chaldeans which did mock them and put them to shame.
